title: tunnel listening JSON
description: Structured stdout payload after local bind for `ssh-cli tunnel ... --json` (or global --output-format json). Process stays alive until --timeout-ms or signal.

vps.description: Registered VPS name used for the tunnel

local_port.description: Local listen port after bind (OS-assigned when the requested port was 0 / ephemeral; never 0 after successful bind — GAP-SSH-TUN-003)

mode.description: Which tunnel is serving. The sibling fields are read differently per mode: under `reverse` the listener is on the SSH server and `local_port` is the port it allocated; under `socks5` the destination is chosen per connection, so `remote_host` is `*` and `remote_port` is 0; under `streamlocal` `remote_host` carries the remote Unix socket path and `remote_port` is 0. Absent in events written before 0.5.4, which can only have been plain local forwards.

remote_host.description: Remote host reached through the SSH channel. `*` under `socks5` (per-connection destination); the remote socket path under `streamlocal`; the local delivery host under `reverse`.

remote_port.description: Remote port reached through the SSH channel. 0 under `socks5` and `streamlocal`, where no single port applies; the local delivery port under `reverse`.

bind.description: Effective local bind address (G-TUN-R06). Lets an agent audit from the contract alone whether the forwarded service was published beyond loopback; `127.0.0.1` is the default.
